content.title: How to watch RBC Heritage 2026: PGA Golf, TV channel
content.text: The 2026 RBC Heritage returns this weekend as one of the PGA Tour’s premier post-Masters events, bringing a loaded field to Harbour Town Golf Links for a signature stop on the schedule. MORE: Unyielding flagstick ruins Rickie Fowler’s unbelievable shot at RBC Heritage Advertisement Apr 17, 2026; Hilton Head, South Carolina, USA; Matt Fitzpatrick and Scottie Scheffler walk the fairway on 18 with their caddies during the second round of the RBC Heritage golf tournament. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images How to Watch RBC Heritage Date: Thursday, April 16, 2026 – Sunday, April 19, 2026 Time: 3:00 PM ET – 6:00 PM ET (CBS); 7:00 AM – 6:00 PM ET (ESPN+) TV Channel: CBS (Main Coverage); ESPN+ (Early Coverage) Live Stream: Fubo (try for free); ESPN Unlimited (watch now) The tournament runs April 16–19, 2026, at Harbour Town Golf Links in Hilton Head Island, South Carolina, continuing its long-standing place on the PGA Tour calendar the week after The Masters. Now designated a Signature Event, the RBC Heritage features a limited, elite field (around 80 players), no cut, and a massive $20 million purse, making it one of the most important non-major events of the season. Defending champion Justin Thomas headlines the field alongside top-ranked players like Scottie Scheffler, Collin Morikawa, and Patrick Cantlay, though Masters winner Rory McIlroy is notably absent this week. – Live Stream RBC Heritage with Fubo – Advertisement – Live Stream RBC Heritage with ESPN Unlimited – Harbour Town presents a unique challenge compared to most PGA Tour stops. The par-71 layout emphasizes precision, shot-making, and course management over raw distance, often leveling the field and rewarding players who excel with irons and around the greens. Past winners like Matt Fitzpatrick (2023), Scottie Scheffler (2024), and Justin Thomas (2025) reflect that trend, with accuracy and control proving key to navigating the tight fairways and small greens. Advertisement With a stacked field, major FedEx Cup implications, and a distinct course style that produces tight leaderboards, the RBC Heritage remains one of the most compelling events of the spring—and a perfect follow-up to the intensity of Augusta.
